one_liner: Single-header C library for Unicode segmentation and OpenType shaping; claimed faster than HarfBuzz, measured 2-160x slower independently.
what_it_does: kb_text_shape.h does text segmentation (paragraph and run direction, script, line, word and grapheme breaks) and OpenType shaping (GSUB/GPOS, the complex-script shapers, font fallback, variable fonts since v2.28) in one stb-style header. The default context API is immediate-mode: push fonts, feed UTF-8 or codepoints between kbts_ShapeBegin and kbts_ShapeEnd, then iterate runs and glyphs (glyph ID, advance, offset in font units, source codepoint index). A lower-level direct API (kbts_ShapeDirect with an explicit shape_config, scratchpad and glyph storage) shapes one already-segmented run. It is not API-compatible with HarfBuzz and does no rasterization, paragraph layout or system font lookup.
how_it_is_fast: Font loading copies the font's tables into a private blob, byte-swaps them in place to native endianness, and precomputes bit matrices of glyph x lookup and glyph x lookup-subtable coverage, so during shaping one bit test decides whether a lookup or subtable can touch a glyph instead of walking coverage tables; each shape_config also builds a glyph x enabled-lookup matrix for the active feature set. Transient shaping state lives in contexts and scratchpads that the caller can size, place in its own memory (fixed-memory placement is supported) and reuse across calls. The cost is paid up front: building those matrices scales with glyphs x lookups, which fits the independent measurement of font loading 40x to 760x slower than HarfBuzz. kbts_LoadFont also accepts a prebuilt kbts blob, so that work can be done once and shipped.
when_to_use: Games, editors-for-display, tools and embedded targets that want shaping plus segmentation from one Zlib-licensed header with no ICU, FriBidi, FreeType or HarfBuzz build, and are willing to give up speed for that.
Programs that must control every allocation: contexts and scratchpads can be placed in caller memory, a custom allocator can be supplied, and KB_TEXT_SHAPE_NO_CRT drops the C runtime.
Display-only rendering of complex scripts (Arabic, Indic v2 fonts, Khmer, Myanmar, Hangul and others) with a small, bundled and trusted font set loaded once at startup or shipped as prebuilt blobs.
Prototyping a text pipeline where the README's model (segment, shape, then hand glyph IDs to stb_truetype or another rasterizer) is enough.
when_not_to_use: Throughput-critical shaping: the only reachable measurements put it behind HarfBuzz on every font tested (2.9x on a Roboto paragraph, 6.6x on Urdu Nastaliq, 160x on Latin text in Gulzar) and about 2x behind raqm/HarfBuzz in a user's test (kb issue #21).

Untrusted or user-supplied fonts: the header says it provides no security guarantee, crash reports on real fonts were fixed during 2025-2026 (issues #43 NotoNastaliqUrdu, #44 SourceSerifVariable-Roman, #61 and #63 glyph insertion), and there is no fuzzing in the repository, unlike HarfBuzz's oss-fuzz coverage.

Text editing, selection, cursor movement or text-extractable PDF: glyphs carry a source codepoint index, but there is no documented HarfBuzz-style cluster merging, explicit bidi control characters (embeddings, overrides, isolates) are not supported, hinting is unsupported, and there is no vertical layout (HarfBuzz's kbts backend rejects vertical directions; issue #64 asking how to do vertical text is open).

Apps that open many fonts or large fonts on demand: each load copies the whole font into dirty memory and builds per-glyph-per-lookup bit matrices (Gulzar load plus one-character shape 235.9 ms against HarfBuzz's 0.31 ms).

Dictionary-based word breaking (CJK), Indic1 fonts (e.g. 'beng' rather than 'bng2'), Zawgyi, the Syriac abbreviation mark, Windows 3.1 Arabic or Thai/Lao PUA fonts, which the header lists as unsupported.

integration.form: header-only (stb-style: define KB_TEXT_SHAPE_IMPLEMENTATION in one translation unit; KB_TEXT_SHAPE_STATIC for static linkage)
integration.dependencies: none (C runtime optional via KB_TEXT_SHAPE_NO_CRT with user KBTS_MALLOC, KBTS_FREE, KBTS_MEMSET, KBTS_MEMCPY)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 or C++ (uses declare-anywhere, so not C89/VC6); GCC 15.2 reports unused-variable and enum-conditional warnings in the current header (issue #91, 2026-10-02), so -Werror builds need flags adjusted
integration.platforms: any: portable scalar C, with SSE2 used only for float rounding when available; MSVC, GCC and clang paths in the header
integration.thread_safety: Header: a shape_config is immutable and can be shared among threads; a shape_scratchpad (and a shape_context) is mutable and must be per thread. HarfBuzz's kbts backend shares one kbts_font and config across threads and hands out per-thread scratchpads.

gotchas: The font stack prefers the most recently pushed font, so fallbacks must be pushed first unless KBTS_SHAPE_CONTEXT_FLAG_FONT_PRIORITY_BOTTOM_TO_TOP is set.
In the context API, kbts_glyph.UserIdOrCodepointIndex is always a codepoint index; your own user ID has to be read back through kbts_ShapeGetShapeCodepoint.
With KB_TEXT_SHAPE_NO_CRT and no custom allocator, the default allocator returns 0; a custom KBTS_MALLOC must also return non-null for zero-size requests (open issue #73).

The API has churned: v2.0 replaced the 1.x API, v2.07 changed kbts_ShapeDirect and struct layouts, and v2.28 added variation-aware *2 entry points; HarfBuzz still pins v2.07 (commit ca6c962) while the header is at v2.28e.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only C/C++ shaper in the category; the catalogued shaping siblings are Rust (Fontations, sigilbuzz, Parley), .NET (SixLabors.Fonts) or JavaScript (text-shaper, rustybuzz-wasm) and all measure against HarfBuzz or its ports. Pick kb over HarfBuzz only for a dependency-free single header with built-in segmentation and trusted fonts, not for speed.
verified_claims_summary: The one opened independent comparison (HarfBuzz maintainer Behdad Esfahbod, discussion #5375, 2025-07-23, HarfBuzz's benchmark-shape and benchmark-font through its kbts backend; CPU, compiler, flags and kb version not stated) found kb slower everywhere: Roboto paragraph 26.5 vs 9.11 ms, Roboto words 38.4 vs 11.3 ms, Amiri 48.3 vs 40.6 ms, Gulzar Urdu 5198 vs 782 ms, Gulzar Latin 4021 vs 24.9 ms, Noto Devanagari 50.5 vs 25.3 ms, and font load 40x to 760x slower; that path converts HarfBuzz buffers and allocates kb glyph storage on every call (src/hb-kbts.cc), which taxes kb somewhat but cannot account for 6.6x to 160x gaps. The author's claim of 4.5x faster on average (HarfBuzz's test suite plus own tests, Ryzen 9 5900HX, clang 20, Linux) exists only in a search snippet with no harness, and no re-measurement of v2.06 ('Faster GSUB and GPOS feature culling'), v2.07 ('Performance improvements') or later versions was found.
status_note: Actively developed (v2.28e, last commit 2026-10-02, 80 commits, about 1.2k stars, 13 open issues, frequent bug-fix releases) and Zlib-licensed, so easy to vendor, but it is a young, single-author shaper whose speed advantage is unproven.
